title: Limit home purchases by foreigners in the Canaries
detail: Reforms in the national parliament to limit home purchases in the Canary Islands by foreigners, based on the islands' status as an EU outermost region (*región ultraperiférica*, RUP) and compatible with EU law; and EU and national changes to allow a Canarian residence law (*Ley Canaria de Residencia*) to manage population growth. Who exactly, and what thresholds, are not given.
c: Limiting purchases by EU citizens is not possible (free movement of capital and establishment); in our estimate only a few countries have exceptions under special protocols to the EU treaties. RUP status (art. 349 TFEU) allows adaptations, but such a limit would need an EU Council decision and would be contested.

title: Regulate holiday lets where housing is under pressure
detail: A national and EU legal basis so the Canaries and their town halls can limit tourist use of homes (*vivienda vacacional*) where pressure on housing is proven, distinguishing occasional use from professional, intensive letting.
c: The Canaries already passed a holiday-let law (Ley 6/2025); a national framework is realistic.
pos: The Canaries could limit holiday lets where they push residents out.
neg: Lost income for holiday-let owners; disputes under EU law.

s.t: Canary Islands Ley 6/2025 on holiday lets (BOE)

title: Stable rentals: tax incentives for small landlords
detail: Better state tax incentives for small landlords who join affordable rental schemes (*alquiler asequible*) with public guarantees for payment and damage; renovation money for empty homes tied to joining those schemes. The programme says nothing about rent caps.
c: The tax incentives are realistic and not expensive.
pos: Small landlords become more willing to let at affordable prices.
neg: A cost to the Treasury; the relief also goes to people who would have let anyway.

title: Tax breaks on La Palma, La Gomera and El Hierro
detail: Keep the 60% income tax (*IRPF*) deduction for La Palma and extend it to La Gomera and El Hierro, plus a 50% cut in employer social security contributions (*bonificación de cuotas*) on those three islands.
c: Tax breaks for La Palma after the volcanic eruption already apply; extending them is cheap.
pos: Helps islands hit by the eruption and by depopulation.
neg: Lost revenue; risk of fake registrations.

title: Protect and update the Canary Islands tax regime (*REF*)
detail: Keep and update the special economic and tax regime (*Régimen Económico y Fiscal de Canarias*, REF) that offsets the islands' permanent disadvantages; stop REF money being counted as ordinary funding for health, education and social services; reject one-sided state reforms.
c: The REF is protected by the Constitution (third additional provision) and the Statute of Autonomy; updates are routine.
pos: Keeps compensation for the extra costs of island life.
neg: The regime costs the national Treasury tax revenue; in our estimate some of the breaks (ZEC, RIC) mainly benefit large companies.

s.t: Ley 19/1994 on the Canary Islands economic and tax regime, REF (BOE)

title: Automatic sharing of migrant reception among regions
detail: When a region of first arrival goes over set thresholds, transfers to other regions (*comunidades autónomas*) start automatically, without case-by-case negotiation; this needs changes to the law.
c: Mandatory distribution was introduced by RDL 2/2025; several regions are challenging it at the Constitutional Court.
pos: A fair sharing of reception between regions.
neg: Regions get obligations without their consent: disputes over powers at the Constitutional Court.

s.t: BOE: Madrid's challenge at the Constitutional Court to RDL 2/2025 on distributing migrant minors

title: Keep the 75% travel discount for residents
detail: Keep the 75% discount on air and sea travel for residents, watch for artificial fare rises, defend direct links between the smaller islands, and have the state cover 100% of the real subsidised cost of shipping goods.
c: The 75% discount is set in the REF; keeping it is realistic (in our estimate about €600–700 million a year).
pos: Affordable travel between the islands and to the mainland.
neg: There is a risk that part of the discount ends up in higher fares; in our estimate it costs about €600–700 million a year.

s.t: Ley 19/1994 on the Canary Islands economic and tax regime, REF (BOE)
